items.definition:
a person or company that is granted a franchise
The franchisee opened a new coffee shop downtown.

the principles, practices, and organization of the Freemasons
He was interested in the history and rituals of freemasonry.

a castrated male horse
The stable had several geldings ready for riding.

a Muslim who has memorized the entire Qur'an
He became a Hafiz after years of dedicated study.

work done skillfully with the hands; a product of one's own efforts
The intricate carving was clearly the handiwork of a master craftsman.

a wrong or inaccurate name or designation
Calling a whale a 'fish' is a common misnomer.

a device or substance that modulates something
The sound system uses a frequency modulator to adjust the signal.

the process of converting something into money
Many online platforms focus on content monetization.

small lump or growth
The doctor found a small nodule on her thyroid.

Yoruba traditional ruler
The Oba of Benin is a revered figure.

father (French, often used for priests)
Père Lachaise is a famous cemetery in Paris.

a trite or unoriginal remark
His speech was full of empty platitudes about hard work.

a therapist who treats mental disorders
She decided to see a psychotherapist to help with her anxiety.

an ornamented staff carried by rulers on ceremonial occasions as a symbol of sovereignty
The queen held the scepter as a symbol of her authority.

a person who is habitually drunk
He was known as a sot, always found at the local tavern.

a stalk or stem, especially the stem of a fungus or seaweed
The mushroom's cap was supported by a thick stipe.

the act of bringing someone or something under domination or control
The empire's goal was the complete subjugation of its neighbors.

the practice by which a woman bears a child for another person or couple
They decided to pursue surrogacy to start their family.

the action of transferring something or the process of being transferred
The transference of skills from one job to another is often beneficial.

the quality of being universal; existing or true everywhere or in all cases
The universality of human rights is a fundamental principle.

a small antechamber or hall leading to a main room
We waited in the vestibule before entering the main hall.

a room or building attached to a church, used as an office, for changing into vestments, etc.
The choir gathered in the vestry before the service.

a small beetle with a long snout, many kinds of which are pests of crops or stored food
The weevil infestation damaged the grain crops.

a person who is fanatical and uncompromising in pursuit of their religious, political, or other ideals
The political zealot refused to listen to any opposing viewpoints.

waste or debris of any kind
The beach was covered in detritus after the storm.

silly nonsense
He was talking absolute drivel after a few drinks.

chemical decomposition by electric current
Electrolysis is used to remove unwanted hair.

a lung condition causing shortness of breath
Smoking can lead to serious conditions like emphysema.

the act of cutting out or removing
The surgeon performed an excision of the tumor.

the retractable fold of skin covering the end of the penis
Circumcision involves the removal of the foreskin.

the study of the Earth's physical processes
Geophysics helps us understand earthquakes and volcanoes.

the science or art of designing, manufacturing, and operating guns
The naval academy offers courses in gunnery.

the bone of the upper arm
He fractured his humerus in the accident.

a person who initiates something
She was the initiator of the new project.

a strong alkaline solution, especially of potassium hydroxide or sodium hydroxide
Lye is used in soap making and drain cleaners.

a person who marauds; a raider
The village was constantly under threat from marauders.

a person's ability to cope well with difficulties or to face a demanding situation in a spirited and resilient way
The challenging project truly tested her mettle.

the use of confrontational or violent methods in support of a political or social cause
The union's militancy led to a prolonged strike.

the act of forcing someone out of a position or office
The CEO's ouster came after a series of financial scandals.

a figure of speech in which apparently contradictory terms appear in conjunction
'Jumbo shrimp' is a classic example of an oxymoron.

the position or office of a university professor
She was awarded a prestigious professorship at the university.

a point of high land that juts out into a large body of water
The lighthouse stood on a rocky promontory overlooking the sea.

a member of certain peoples of very short stature; or, an unusually small example of its kind
The pygmy marmoset is one of the smallest monkeys in the world.

the quality or state of being relevant
The relevancy of the data to our study is crucial.

a channel for surplus water from a dam or reservoir
The dam's spillway was opened to release excess water.

a state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility
He awoke from his drunken stupor with a pounding headache.

a person who is the first to do something or go somewhere
Marie Curie was a trailblazer in the field of science.

a feeling of fear or agitation about something that may happen
He felt a sense of trepidation before his job interview.

the principles or policy of forming or joining a trade union
Unionism has played a significant role in workers' rights.

the act of urinating
Frequent urination can be a symptom of certain conditions.

a spoken word, statement, or vocal sound
Every utterance from the speaker was carefully considered.

the student who has the highest academic rank in a graduating class
The valedictorian delivered an inspiring speech at graduation.

a white, translucent form of gypsum, often carved
The statue was carved from pure alabaster.

a state of controlled, temporary loss of sensation or awareness
The patient was given general anaesthesia before the surgery.

an irregular heartbeat
He was diagnosed with a mild heart arrhythmia.

a soft, silvery-white metallic element
Barium is used in some medical imaging procedures.

an aluminum ore
Bauxite is the main source of aluminum.

the unintended and unwelcome consequences of a policy or action
The government's new policy caused significant public blowback.

A ceremonial pipe.
The chief offered the calumet as a sign of peace.

Decaying flesh.
Vultures feed on carrion left by predators.

An attitude of superiority.
His tone was full of condescension, making her feel small.

The choice and use of words and phrases.
The poet's diction was precise and evocative.

A mournful poem, especially for the dead.
The poet wrote a beautiful elegy for his lost friend.

A person who studies insects.
The entomologist identified the rare butterfly species.
